chapter: Casimir, Bigard and Allen's brass band
title: John Casimir loved brass bands; his brothers
summary: John Casimir read a little, bragged, preferred brass bands to better-paying dances; brothers Sam and William were in Navy bands.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: John? John could read a little, yeah. Yeah, he could read a little. He used to brag, you know.
Yeah. About how he could read, but I don't think he was a... He used to say.

But he loved it to John, I tell you about John. John loved it to play in them brass bands. Oh, I know. Now if John had a job somewhere playing, a dance in a dance playing, they'd buy ten dollars, and they're going to make three dollars out there in the brass band, he'd soon go out there in that brass band. Oh, of course. Just to blow that clarinet out in that street. There'd never be another one like him. Yeah, no, indeed. John was something to us, I tell you. He was a terrible little fella. He wasn't no musicianist though with his other brothers though. He had two brothers there, there was two British musicians. Could they play?
They both was in the Navy bands, John's brothers.
Well, I heard Sam on record, but I never heard much of Bill. No, right. William. I think he made some records, but they don't sound as good as...
